evidence: All five lesson objectives are addressed: parallel lines, perpendicular lines, bisecting a line segment, 90° angle, and 60° angle each have their own dedicated section.
The pack is explicitly labelled for JSS1 Third Term construction work, matching the curriculum target exactly.
Each section ends with practice questions that directly test the stated objective (e.g. 'Construct a 90° angle at a point C on a line AB').
objective_curriculum_alignment.rationale: Every objective listed in the lesson plan is covered with explanation, worked example, and practice. There are no missing objectives and no extraneous topics introduced.

evidence: The pack follows the same sequence as the lesson presentation: parallel lines → perpendicular lines → bisection → 90° → 60°, matching the teacher's order exactly.

The methods match what the teacher used: set square and ruler for parallel and perpendicular lines, compasses for bisection and angle construction — consistent with 'mathematical set' as instructional material.

The pack is text-and-figure based rather than a hands-on follow-along with a teacher at the board; the lesson was built around the teacher demonstrating and students replicating simultaneously, a dynamic the take-home pack cannot fully replicate.
taught_lesson_alignment.rationale: Sequence, tools, and methods all match the taught lesson closely. The only gap is that the lesson centred on simultaneous teacher-demonstration-and-student-replication, which a written pack can approximate but not fully reproduce.

evidence: The bisection section correctly states that the compass opening must exceed half the length of AB, and explains why (arcs would not cross otherwise) — this is mathematically accurate.
The 60° construction correctly identifies that equal radii produce an equilateral triangle with 60° angles at each vertex, which is the standard geometric justification.
The 90° construction correctly distinguishes two compass settings and explains why the second must be wider than the first — no conceptual errors detected across any of the five sections.
scope_conceptual_correctness.rationale: All five constructions are explained with correct geometry and no errors in scope; the pack stays within JSS1 construction boundaries and every mathematical claim made is accurate.

evidence: Steps are numbered and clearly sequenced in each section, making it easy for a student working alone to follow without a teacher present.
The 'Check your work' section provides full model answers keyed to each practice question, giving students a self-assessment tool appropriate for independent home use.

Figure references (fig-01 through fig-14) are used throughout but the actual figures are described only in italicised placeholder text, meaning students at home cannot see the visual support the text repeatedly relies on — this is a meaningful usability gap for JSS1 learners.
clarity_usefulness.rationale: The writing is clear, age-appropriate, and well-structured for independent study, and the answer key adds real value; however, the heavy reliance on figures that are described but not actually rendered limits how much a student working alone can benefit from the pack.
